finding.claim: Negative amt lets any authenticated user drain any account via transfer_funds
finding.sink: UPDATE acct SET bal = bal +/- ? at actions.php:17-18

trace.note: sender bal = bal - amt; amt=-500 credits attacker
target bal = bal + amt; to=<victim> is debited 500

finding.guards_checked: None: no numeric or positive check on amt, no ownership or existence check on to, no balance check; CSRF check does not gate this path

verdict.guard_found: check_csrf (actions.php:4-6) is the only control on this path, but its bool result is discarded as a bare statement at actions.php:16, so it gates nothing. No numeric or positive check on $_POST['amt'] (line 17-18), no existence or ownership check on $_POST['to'], and no balance check. verify_csrf (lines 8-13) is not called on this path.
verdict.reason: transfer_funds at actions.php:16 discards the check_csrf result, and actions.php:17-18 subtract and add the unvalidated $_POST['amt'] to the session user and to $_POST['to'], so a negative amt debits the victim; the caveat is that the router that calls transfer_funds is not in this directory, so the attacker's HTTP reachability is inferred from the $_POST usage rather than shown.

finding.claim: CSRF check on transfer_funds is computed but its result is ignored, so state-changing transfer runs without a valid token
finding.source: Cross-site form or auto-submitting page causing victim browser to POST to transfer endpoint

trace.note: check_csrf(...) return value dropped; verify_csrf not used

finding.guards_checked: hash_equals is constant-time and correct, but unenforced; update_profile at line 22 uses verify_csrf so the bug is specific to transfer_funds. Exploitability depends on session cookie SameSite config, which is not visible in this file (Lax default blocks cross-site POST cookies)
finding.repro: Victim with active session loads attacker page that auto-submits POST to transfer endpoint with to=<attacker>&amt=<balance>; no token required

verdict.guard_found: check_csrf at actions.php:4-5 returns a bool, but its result is discarded by the bare call at actions.php:16, so it is not enforced. verify_csrf (actions.php:8-13, which exits on failure) is not called in transfer_funds. The only other control is session_start (actions.php:2), which does not check the token. SameSite cookie handling is not visible in this directory and is the only possible mitigation outside the code.
verdict.reason: The check_csrf() result at actions.php:16 is a bare statement, so debit and credit at actions.php:17-18 run with no token enforcement, while update_profile at actions.php:22 correctly uses verify_csrf. An anonymous cross-site attacker can reach this by making a logged-in victim's browser POST to the endpoint, and the only mitigation, a SameSite cookie default, is not in the code and does not remove the defect. The transfer_funds caller is not in this directory, so the reachable route is unverified, and SameSite=Lax would block the auto-submitting cross-site POST in some browsers.

finding.claim: Transfer has no balance check and no transaction; overdraft, partial failure, and nonexistent recipient cause integrity loss

trace.note: debit with no balance check; balance can go negative
credit may match zero rows if to does not exist, destroying funds
no BEGIN/COMMIT; failure between statements leaves debit without credit

finding.guards_checked: None: no balance check, no recipient existence check, no transaction
finding.repro: POST amt=<more than balance>&to=<any>; or POST to=<nonexistent id> to destroy funds from sender

verdict.guard_found: None effective. The only control on this path is check_csrf() at actions.php:16, but it is called as a bare statement and its bool return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No balance check, amount validation, recipient existence check, or transaction exists in transfer_funds (actions.php:15-19).
verdict.reason: The debit at actions.php:17 has no balance or amount check and the credit at actions.php:18 silently matches zero rows for a nonexistent `to`, with no transaction wrapping the two statements, so an authenticated user (the $_SESSION['uid'] identity) can overdraw or destroy funds; caveat: no caller of transfer_funds exists in this directory, so reachability depends on an unseen dispatcher, and the candidate missed the more severe fact that the CSRF check at actions.php:16 is a no-op.
